name: Implement
description: Implements every spec on the rail in one run: plan, implement, review and verify, fixing failures until the checks pass.

params.prompt: Plan the frozen ticket requirements for OpenSpec change {{run.changeId}}. Use the bound official fast-forward skill. Author complete proposal, design, delta specs and actionable tasks. Propose existing repository verification commands for repositories with no configured checks. Return confidence, question (empty when none), and verification [{repositoryId,command,args,cwd?}]. When revisiting low confidence, investigate the missing repository evidence before asking again. Context and human answers: {{history.text}}

Implement every approved task for change {{run.changeId}} using the bound official apply skill. Preserve proposal, design and specs; only tick tasks you completed. Report summary and incomplete task descriptions. If a task cannot be finished because of a host precondition or environment blocker outside this change (for example the sandbox forbids starting a local server, a credential or tool is missing), keep the work done, leave that task unchecked and return the structured blocker (kind, command, cwd, evidence, requiredAction). A failing test, a test you cannot make pass, or unexpected browser or tool behaviour is NOT a host blocker: change the test or the implementation instead. The host confirms a blocker by running its own verification before ending the run; a failure it reproduces comes back as a correction. Prior execution evidence and human answers: {{history.text}}

Review change {{run.changeId}} read-only against all approved artifacts and frozen ticket acceptance criteria. Inspect real code and the host verification evidence: {{outputs.verify}}. Return approved, summary, issues, score (0-100), and aspects. Acceptance policy: approved == true; issues must be empty; score >= 70; type_correctness >= 60; pattern_adherence >= 60; test_coverage >= 60; security >= 75; architectural_alignment >= 60. For any rejection or below-threshold score, explain the concrete unmet requirement and actionable repair in summary and issues; passing commands do not prove every acceptance obligation. Prior execution: {{history.text}}

set.latestReview: No reviewer findings for the current verified candidate. Diagnose the current host verification failure first.

params.prompt: Correct the reported implementation, test or review failure for change {{run.changeId}} using the bound apply skill and preserving approved artifacts. Read failureSummary, command, cwd, exitCode and evidenceId first; use read_verification_evidence for truncated evidence. If Host verification is valid, repair the concrete rejected review obligation or below-threshold aspect instead of only rerunning green commands. Acceptance policy: approved == true; issues must be empty; score >= 70; type_correctness >= 60; pattern_adherence >= 60; test_coverage >= 60; security >= 75; architectural_alignment >= 60. Reproduce the exact focused failure, inspect the assertion and tested code, then apply the smallest repair that preserves the required behavior. An unchanged filename does not prove an unrelated failure. A mandatory test inside the admitted workspace may receive a proven formatting/compatibility repair while retaining every required guard. Report diagnosis, focused commands with original exit codes, repair and unresolved failures in summary and incomplete. If the cause is a host precondition or environment blocker outside this change, make no edits and return the structured blocker (kind, command, cwd, evidence, requiredAction): the host ends the run with your required action. Any other unchanged correction stops this run even when host checks pass. Do not make unrelated edits merely to change the candidate hash. Host verification: {{outputs.verify}}. Latest review findings for this candidate: {{run.latestReview}}. Prior execution: {{history.text}}

name: Freestyle
description: Hands the spec straight to the model with full freedom — no pipeline, it works like a regular coding agent, then verify + refine until green.

params.goal: Stop only when actual behavioral evidence proves every frozen acceptance criterion is implemented across every selected ticket and repository. Passing baseline checks alone is insufficient.

name: SDD Quick (OpenSpec)
description: Quick spec-driven OpenSpec lifecycle for small contract-governed changes: prepare artifacts, apply and test, validate through the CLI, then archive.

name: Flow → Spec
description: Derives the spec of code built in a Flow session: writes the OpenSpec change from the diff and the conversation, verifies it, reviews coverage and archives it.

set.latestFindings: Host verification failed for the current candidate: {{outputs.check}}

params.prompt: Review OpenSpec change {{run.changeId}}, derived from code that already exists in this worktree (a Flow session built it with the user). Judge whether the derived proposal, design, delta specs and checked tasks describe the real code faithfully: no invented requirements, nothing material left out. Derivation coverage measured by Core (every changed file must appear in design.md "## Blast radius"): {{outputs.derive.derivation}}. Treat EVERY file in unexplainedFiles as an issue. Inspect the real code and the host verification evidence: {{outputs.check}}. Every issue must be actionable by a fixer (code or tests) or by the deriver (artifacts): name the file and what must change. Return approved, summary, issues (empty when none) and score (0-100).

Correct the code a Flow session built for OpenSpec change {{run.changeId}} so the review can approve it. Findings to resolve (the reviewer's structured verdict, or the failing host verification): {{run.latestFindings}}. Fix the defects the findings name. Add or extend the tests the findings ask for; creating a test file is allowed for that. Tag every test that demonstrates an ADDED or MODIFIED requirement of the change's delta specs with `[spec:<capability>/<requirement-slug>]` in its title. Never expand scope: no new features, effects, options or behaviour. Do not edit anything under openspec/: Core re-derives proposal, design, specs and tasks from the code after your turn, so a finding about the artifacts needs no code change. Revert code only when a finding says the behaviour was unrequested AND contradicts a stated Non-Goal. Return summary and incomplete (each finding you could not resolve, with the reason).
